Management of Turner:

  • •Puberty induction: done in collaboration with paedsS endocrinologist.

Breast development: in 2 stages.

  • -1st stage = low dose estrogen to avoid irregular breast development either oral or transdermal.
  • -2nd stage = progesterone after 2 years of estrogen.
  • •Fertility option:
  1. 1.Fertility preservation if ovulating like in mosaic.
  2. 2.Ovum donation.
  3. 3.Adoption.

2.MRKH:

  • -P0 Amenorrhea
  • -20 SSC are normal

MRI: is gold standard Test

  • -Uterus absent
  • -Ovaries present

No need of HRT.

1.CAIS: complete androgen insensitivity syndrome.

  • -Absent uterus
  • -Breast developed.
  • -Public/Axillary sparse – Tanner stage 2,3.

Treatment:

  • •ERT (no need of progestogen) after gonadectomy
  • •Gonadectomy after puberty at 18yrs, risk of malignancy 2%

2.SWYer’s Syndrome:

  • -Absent SRY gene on Y Chromosome
  • -External genitalia phenotypically – Female
  • -Ambiguous Gentelia, clitoromegaly
  • -Infantile uterus
